originalTitle: Shiprocket draws Goldman Sachs, HDFC MF, SBI MF and others to Rs 727 crore anchor round ahead of IPO
simplifiedContent: Shiprocket, a company that helps with e-commerce, is planning to sell its shares to the public for the first time. Before this happens, the company has already collected Rs 727.41 crore from big investors like Goldman Sachs and some Indian mutual funds. The company wants to collect a total of Rs 1,617.48 crore from its share sale, and the price of each share will be between Rs 92 and Rs 97. The money collected will be used to grow the company, improve its technology, pay off debts, and make new purchases. This is important because it shows that big investors are interested in Shiprocket, which could affect how well its share sale does.

originalTitle: Gold edges higher near two-month peak ahead of US inflation data
simplifiedContent: The price of gold has risen to a level it hasn't seen in about two months. This is happening because investors are waiting to see what the latest inflation numbers from the US will be, which could give them a hint about what the Federal Reserve will do next with interest rates. Recently, there was a report that showed fewer jobs were created than expected, which makes investors think the Federal Reserve might not raise interest rates in September. As a result, the price of gold has gone up, and it's also being helped by worries about global events that are keeping oil prices high. This matters because gold is often seen as a safe investment, so when investors are feeling uncertain, they may buy more gold, which can drive up its price.

originalTitle: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Wednesday
simplifiedContent: Here's what you need to know about what happened in the stock market: the Indian stock market went down, with two important indexes, Sensex and Nifty, falling by 388 and 112 points respectively. This happened because the price of crude oil is going up and the value of the Indian rupee is going down, which makes investors nervous. Some analysts think that if the market falls below 24,400, it could go down even more. This decline is also affected by worries about global politics and upcoming news about inflation. Overall, these factors will likely influence what happens in the stock market tomorrow.

originalTitle: Shiprocket raises  ₹727 crore from anchor investors ahead of IPO launch on Wednesday
simplifiedContent: Shiprocket, an e-commerce company, has received ₹727 crore from important investors before its initial public offering (IPO) starts on August 12. An IPO is when a company sells its shares to the public for the first time. The company wants to raise a total of ₹1,617 crore to improve its marketing and technology, pay back loans, and possibly buy other companies. The shares will be sold at a fixed price between ₹92 and ₹97. This is a significant step for Shiprocket as it prepares to go public and raise the funds it needs to grow and develop its business.

originalTitle: Landmark Cars net profit nearly doubles to  ₹14.5 crore in Q1; revenue rises 22%
simplifiedContent: Landmark Cars, a company that sells cars, made a profit of ₹14.5 crore in the first quarter of the year, which is almost double what they made last year. They also made more money overall, with their revenue increasing by 22%. A big part of their revenue came from selling Mercedes-Benz cars, which made up 38% of their sales. The company's stock price went up by 15.4% in June and 10.2% in July, which means the value of the company's shares increased. This matters because it shows that the company is doing well and making more money, which could be a good sign for people who own or are thinking of buying their stock.

originalTitle: Sebi proposes wider FPI access to non-agri commodity derivatives
simplifiedContent: The stock market regulator, Sebi, has suggested allowing Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) to trade in more types of non-agricultural commodity derivatives. Currently, FPIs are only allowed to trade in certain non-agricultural commodities like crude oil and natural gas, but only if they are settled in cash. This change could give FPIs more options to invest in. This matters because it could bring more money into the Indian market from foreign investors. By allowing FPIs to trade in more commodities, Sebi is trying to make the Indian market more attractive to foreign investors.
